Synthetic Sequence Study
Example Author One and Example Author Two
Example University
Corresponding author: Example Author Two, Example Learning Lab.
Accepted at Example Conference 2026.
We study machine learning methods for time series forecasting and compare prediction errors.
The experiments use synthetic sequences and report limitations of short training histories.

First public release v1: 15 January 2026, arXiv.
Abstract: Time series combine fast fluctuations with long-term structure. A single encoder fails to adapt its representation when the regime changes. We introduce a temporal mixture of experts to route each sequence to specialized predictors.
Method: A temporal encoder receives 96 time steps from 8 sensors. The router uses the encoded state to choose two of four experts. Expert predictions are combined by routing weights. Training minimizes mean squared error with an adaptive weight for short versus long windows. At inference the router and experts produce a 24-step forecast.
Experiments: On synthetic sequences this model reduces mean squared error by 8% compared to a single temporal encoder. Removing the router removes the improvement. The evaluation is a synthetic offline experiment.

contributions.description: 编码输入序列的状态，从四个专家中选出两个，用路由权重融合专家预测。

contributions.description: 训练时平衡短期与长期窗口的均方误差，输出未来24步预测。

reading.summary: 通过状态路由选择时序专家，结合自适应训练权重实现多时间尺度预测。
